messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate on streaming-decode cluster (us-west-2). 75% of requests returning 5xx or dropped. GPU OOM patterns seen in last 3m. Auto-pager -> severity P1. See telemetry: https://telemetry.redwood/cluster/streaming-decode
morgan: I'm on it, taking pager. linking @emma for runtime help and @neil for infra.
emma: thanks. quick question — is this a single node or across multiple hosts? telemetry shows spike on node-pool-dc4.
neil: multiple nodes in that pool showing CUDA OOMs and container restarts. suspect runaway generation from mis-set max_tokens on some client requests.
delta: we have an active customer ticket from corpX reporting request drops starting ~5309998700. They sent a transcript w/ long system prompt.
morgan: priority checklist: 1) isolate affected pool 2) throttle / enforce max_tokens server-side 3) roll traffic to fallback model variant 4) customer-facing update. I'll coord.
emma: trying soft-contain first — enable per-connection token cap and KV eviction on the pool. Running hotpatch:
```
rdctl cluster update --pool streaming-decode-dc4 --config '{"enforce_max_tokens":true, "max_tokens_override":512, "kv_evict":true}'
```
ops-bot: job rdctlclusterupdate-232 started on controller-3, patch queued.
morgan: also add runtime fallback route for streaming requests: route to smallest-compatible model variant (quantized) when mem spike detected. emma can you attach safe variant?
emma: attaching rn, creating canary that returns through quantized-v2 when OOM threshold exceeded. config snippet:
```
"fallback_policy": {
  "on_error":"fallback_quantized_v2",
  "oom_threshold": 0.15
}
```
neil: infra note — container restarts look like: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:34Z] cudaMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. attempted 14.7GB, free 1.2GB
[2026-03-15T10:12:35Z] container runtime: restart count 3
[2026-03-15T10:12:35Z] kernel: oom_killer invoked
```
morgan: good. emma, once fallback is live, we should force-quarantine the affected pool to prevent new allocations until we confirm stable. set autoscale to 0 for pool streaming-decode-dc4.
emma: done: `rdctl pool set-autoscale streaming-decode-dc4 0` 
ops-bot: autoscale set, draining incoming new connections from lb-target streaming-decode-dc4.
delta: corpX updated ticket: they saw a client header with max_tokens=20000 (!!!!!) and content that triggers long generation loops. sharing sample header (redacted):
```
X-Client-Max-Tokens: 20000
X-Prompt-Length: 4k
```
morgan: ack. that's the misconfig. Need to mitigate at edge: reject requests with excessive header or coerce down. Can we push a router rule?
neil: pushing router rule now to reject if X-Client-Max-Tokens > 2000 and return 4xx with guidance. `routerctl add-rule --name cap-max-tokens --expr 'hdr(X-Client-Max-Tokens) > 2000' --action reject`
ops-bot: router rule cap-max-tokens deployed to edge-01, edge-02, edge-03.
emma: fallback stable for 3m, error rate dropped from 75% -> 12%. KV evict and enforced max_tokens also reduced memory pressure.
delta: corpX notified: we're throttling abnormal token requests and rolling fallback. Will update them with ETA for full fix.
morgan: assign followups: 1) support to reach out to top 10 customers with high token use and ask for client-side cap (delta) 2) runtime to add server-side max_token hard cap and telemetry alert (emma) 3) infra to investigate why OOM thresholds didn't trigger earlier (neil).
emma: filed ENG-RUNTIME-4621 for server-side hard cap + unit tests. saving reproducer to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/5309998888/repro.tar.gz
neil: infra triage — node-level memory fragmentation observed. kernel logs show frequent allocations preceding OOMs. filing INFRA-3072. also we'll schedule rolling kernel update to address fragmentation.
morgan: customer impact summary for ops: corpX (~1.2% of traffic) saw ~40% of their streaming requests dropped during the window 5309998600-5309999000. multiple other customers saw elevated latency / errors. preparing bulletin.
delta: updating corpX PRD with timeline and mitigation steps. will propose server-side max as recommended fix for them.
emma: small postmortem note: reproducible with a single request where client sets max_tokens extremely high and prompt leads to self-referential generation -> runaway. added a short-term guard in decoder to break on token emission rate > 200 tokens/s per connection.
morgan: handoff to next oncall @neil at 5309999100. neil — you're owning post-incident followups and customer comms until wrap.
neil: taking it. I'll coordinate with emma on runtime patch and file RCA. quick status: fallback active, router rule deployed, pool quarantined, autoscale disabled. recovering.
morgan: thanks team. I'll draft the incident summary and publish to #incidents postmortems later. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: INCIDENT P1 closed by morgan at 5309999128 (mitigations applied, traffic stabilized).
